subject: RFI: Dedicated Deployment Scaling Playbook & GPU Portfolio for NimbusAI
messages:
From: Jules Martin <jules.martin@nimbus.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus AI Procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RFP - Dedicated inference capacity questionnaire (NimbusAI)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this RFP — attached is our detailed questionnaire focused on dedicated capacity sizing, expected throughput (p50/p95 per-tenant), preferred GPU families, and reservation phasing. High-level context: we plan to move a mix of production LLM traffic (chat and embeddings) to dedicated pools in Q3 and want concrete guidance on GPU family fit, tail-latency tradeoffs, and a recommended reservation phasing (pilot -> run-rate -> burst).

Key items we flagged in the questionnaire:
- Preferred GPU families to recommend for 13B vs 70B models (latency vs $/token tradeoffs)
- Expected sustained p95 tokens/s per tenant and burst multipliers
- How Redwood maps model quantization and KV cache behavior to slotting and packing efficiency
- Fallback policies and how they affect tail latency during burst events

Can you confirm you received the attachment (nimbus_rfp_questionnaire.xlsx) and whether Redwood can provide a draft fitment workbook and short kickoff call next week? Ideally we'd get a workbook and a short written response within 3 business days, with a deeper sizing workshop to follow.

Best,
Jules
Procurement Lead, Nimbus AI

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jules Martin <jules.martin@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Nimbus AI Procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - Dedicated inference capacity questionnaire (NimbusAI)

Jules — thanks, received and uploaded to our intake folder. Attaching a short "fitment workbook" (gpu_fitment_workbook_v3.xlsx) that we'll use to map your load profile to GPU families. Two quick clarification questions before we draft the detailed response:

1) Can you confirm the mix of models (approx % of traffic) that will be 13B vs 70B vs embeddings? The workbook assumes 60/25/15 as a starting point but we can change.
2) For burst windows, are you expecting synchronous user-facing bursts (chat p95 constraint 200–300ms) or asynchronous background batch (higher latency ok)?

Meeting proposal: 30 minutes on Mon 2028-03-26 10:00-10:30 PT to walk the workbook and initial recommendations. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Attachment: gpu_fitment_workbook_v3.xlsx (worksheet: runrate, burst, slotting notes)

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Nimbus RFP - internal: recommended GPU portfolio & reservation phasing (notes)

Team — quick internal note to capture recommended approach before the Monday kickoff. I'm drafting the workbook answers but wanted your checks on the GPU mix and reservation phasing. Summary of recommended posture:

- Pilot (Q3 month 1–2): 2–4 A100-80GB hosts for 13B chat + 1 H100-80GB node for 70B validation. Purpose: validate p95 latency at expected run-rate, tune batching/kv cache.
- Run-rate (Q3 month 3 onward): move to a blended pool: 60% L4 / A100 for 13B production (quantized fp4/INT8 where quality tolerates), 40% H100-family reserved slots for 70B models and critical low-latency tails. Use autoscaling buffer of 1.25x run-rate and slot-level pre-warming.
- Burst lanes: reserve 10–15% capacity as burst lanes (pre-warmed, cheaper GPU mix acceptable if p95 relaxed). For synchronous chat bursts that need 250–300ms p95 we recommend routing to H100 reserved fast-path or fallback to a slightly smaller model on A100 with aggressive KV prefix caching.

Operational notes:
- Packing: enable per-tenant slotting to avoid noisy neighbors; pack smaller embedding tasks into L4 family instances.
- Quantization: recommend customer-level quantization policy; 13B models on INT8/fp4 for cost sensitivity, 70B kept FP16/HFQ where quality matters.
- Metrics: we will surface token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and per-route KV hit-rate.

Questions for Marcus/Priyom: what are the short-run implications on unit cost if we move 40% of 13B traffic from FP16 (A100) -> INT8 (L4)? I sketched 18–24% token cost savings but need confirmation. Also, Priyom, can you draft the reservation phasing language (contractual months, burst credits, early-termination credits)?

- Olga

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jules Martin <jules.martin@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Nimbus AI Procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Mar 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - Dedicated inference capacity questionnaire (NimbusAI)

Hi Jules — appreciated the quick turn. Attached is our formal RFI response (redwood_dedicated_fitment_response.pdf) and the populated workbook (gpu_fitment_workbook_v3.xlsx). Highlights in the package:

- GPU portfolio recommendation: pilot on A100-80GB + single H100 node for 70B; run-rate blend with L4-optimized slots for quantized 13B workloads and H100 reserved for critical low-latency 70B paths.
- Throughput targets & sizing: workbook includes p50/p95 per-tenant token/s assumptions, packing efficiency at three levels (conservative/expected/optimistic), and slot counts per reservation tier.
- Reservation phasing language: 3-month pilot credit, then 12-month run-rate commitment with quarterly burst credits (documented in section 4). We propose a 1.15x baseline autoscale buffer for SLA-backed p95 targets and explicit fallback policies to guarantee availability during regional constraints.
- Cost delta: estimated 20% token cost savings by moving quantizable 13B traffic from FP16 A100 to INT8 L4 in steady-state. We included unit economics by token buckets in the workbook.

Next steps I propose:
1) 30-min sizing workshop (Mon 2028-03-26 10:00 PT) to validate assumptions in the workbook.
2) If validated, we prepare a draft term sheet for a pilot PO + run-rate reservation schedule within 5 business days.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_fitment_response.pdf, gpu_fitment_workbook_v3.xlsx
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nimbus-rfp (same as earlier)

Let me know if you want us to include sample SLA language on tail-latency credits.

Thanks — Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_dedicated_fitment_response.pdf (summary + workbook), gpu_fitment_workbook_v3.xlsx (populated)
